calls.title: PR Reviews
calls.summary: Key decisions included adopting a full resync approach for attribute synchronization, allowing complete regeneration of identifiers and queries to enhance clarity and reduce bugs. The team discussed using JSON blobs for attribute storage in the data warehouse, preventing costly schema migrations while allowing nullable columns. They emphasized the importance of maintaining stable IDs for experiment assignment to ensure data recovery if attributes change. Plans for enhancing the event forwarder and job queue involved reviewing legacy code and improving reliability with Kafka integration. Additionally, the proposal for materialized views aimed to facilitate usage tracking and data retention with a 30-day limit. The meeting also addressed API route management to enhance security and streamline request handling.
calls.keywords: read-only, event forwarder, attribute syncing, usage tracking, AI assistant skills, API permission checks
calls.action_items:
**Nhat Ho**
Block editing of experiment queries and remove delete buttons from the UI to enforce read-only status and preserve data integrity (00:29)
Remove redundant warning logic related to Avro schema updates that are no longer necessary due to simplified syncing approach (03:24)
Clean up branch logic in sync event forwarder code by simplifying to resync all identifiers, experiment assignment queries, and fact tables on any attribute change (07:05)
Add descriptive annotations to fact tables explaining their read-only state and that they are auto-generated by the event forwarder to improve user clarity (23:07)
Remove obsolete job queue functions and simplify the provisioning refresh flow, including maintaining a one-minute hard-coded delay for fact table refresh after event forwarder provisioning (16:37)

**Jeremy Dorn**
Refactor sync logic to perform full synchronization rather than complex conditional updates when attribute schemas change, simplifying maintenance and reliability (05:53)
Validate that sync functions handle errors internally with try-catch blocks to prevent error propagation during attribute syncing operations (20:51)
Remove unnecessary update methods for fact tables now marked as read-only to prevent unintended modifications (22:04)
Review and improve API route permission checks and route handling to optimize security and simplify usage, including exploring runtime versus compile-time route management (39:11)

**Michael Knowlton**
Set up a materialized view in ClickHouse aggregating forwarded usage data per hour and configure TTL for raw event data to optimize query performance and storage management (27:51)
Verify whether batch events are sent individually or aggregated to Kafka to ensure accurate usage counting and tracking (29:53)

**Omar Elshaikh**
Review and test AI-assistant skill implementations, focusing on the security dispatcher and experiment skills, to ensure safe and effective functionality (37:41)
Explore simplifying API request handling by invoking route handlers as pure functions, bypassing Express.js middleware for better maintainability and security (44:06)

**Lillia Jackson**
Add detailed self-comments and tagged sections to PR to facilitate more focused and comprehensive feedback during review sessions (30:39)
